divergences.old: Kibana using the Elasticsearch API key whenever it has none of its own: TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY, then TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY, then the stored kibana.apiKey, then the stored elasticsearch.apiKey
divergences.toil: A Kibana connection uses an Elasticsearch connection's apiKey only when it names it in apiKeyFrom, with the env tier beating the file tier and Kibana's own key winning a tie. The one exception keeps the env chain the contract records: Kibana's default connection takes TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY when TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY isn't set. A stored Elasticsearch key is never borrowed unpaired. The key still goes only to the Kibana connection's own baseUrl, and meta.context.shared says when it was borrowed
divergences.why: Cross-area credentials need an explicit pairing (maintainer decision 7 on #68): a credential goes only to the connection it's configured on, or to one the user paired it with.

divergences.old: With no key: "Kibana credentials not configured. Set kibana.apiKey, or elasticsearch.apiKey to share the Elasticsearch key." A 401 or 403 on the borrowed key added "set ..._KIBANA_API_KEY or kibana.apiKey"
divergences.toil: NOT_CONFIGURED, "Kibana credentials not configured on connection <name>.", with a fix naming TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY, toil connections login and the apiKeyFrom pairing; nothing is sent. A 401 or 403 on a borrowed key names the Elasticsearch connection it came from and says to give the Kibana connection its own key with toil connections login <name>, or TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY for the default connection
divergences.why: The recorded advice doesn't work in toil: a stored elasticsearch.apiKey is shared only through apiKeyFrom, and a plaintext kibana.apiKey in a config file is refused (Secrets), so each error names what does work.

divergences.old: The Kibana space from --space or the connection taken as any non-empty text and encoded into the /s/<space> path prefix
divergences.toil: A space ID holding /, , ?, #, % or a control character is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, however it arrives: --space, the MCP field, the dossier, an env var or the connection setting. Rule IDs are still encoded as one path segment
divergences.why: Kibana space IDs are lowercase letters, digits, _ and -, so a value with path syntax in it names no space.
